$comment: Starter golden dataset for `recallum-admin eval`. Grow it with real queries your agents got wrong: every regression you fix should leave a query behind. Tags name the retrieval class a query exercises so tuning changes show per-class effects.
$language_experiment: The es-*/en-* corpus keys and the four <content>-<query> tags (es-es, es-en, en-en, en-es) form a 2x2 measuring the English-only memory policy. Each fact is stored once and queried in BOTH languages, so es-es vs es-en and en-en vs en-es are within-fact comparisons -- the language is the only variable. The two halves use disjoint topics so an English query cannot accidentally retrieve the Spanish half. Read it as: en-en is the new happy path; es-en is what the transition costs while pre-policy Spanish memories are still stored; en-es is what half-compliance costs when an agent stores English but keeps querying in the user's language; es-es is the pre-policy control. CAVEAT: Spanish and English technical vocabulary share Latin roots and the trigram leg is character-based, so cognates hand the cross-language tags a partial lexical freebie. Treat es-en and en-es as an OPTIMISTIC bound on the mixed-language penalty, not a measurement of it. REMOVING or REWORDING a corpus row strands the previously seeded memory: it stays active but is no longer mapped to a key, so it competes for top-k slots as an unlabelled distractor. Prune the eval user when you do either. Adding rows and changing importance or category strand nothing.
